## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b898a12ddc83a9a886e01f6bec77acf2386c7700`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/area-lease.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/coordinator.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/dispatch-runbook.md + none

Read, not reviewed (outside the diff, all on `main`): `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md`, `references/triage-duties.md`, `references/seat-post-protocol.md`, `references/rest-channel.md`, `references/platform-readings.md`, `references/lanes/cloud.md`, `references/lanes/director.md`, `.claude/agents/os-dev.md`, `scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs`, `scripts/pm/fleet-write/dispatch.mjs` and `ops.mjs` (header text), `.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml`. Inputs: card #34625 body and its one comment (claim 6937847756), the PR body, its three files, the net diff against merge base 97defd6067, both PR comments, and the 48 check-runs on the head.

### ① Derived judgments

The diff is three rules files, +10/−10, no code, no schema, no published surface. What it changes is who may do what:

- Line budget — right. Counted from the git objects at the head: dispatch-runbook 246 lines (ceiling 246), coordinator 49 (49), area-lease 71 (71); widest line in each file is 120 bytes, the ten added lines are 111 to 120 bytes. The gate is `scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs` (its `CEILINGS` map and the 120-byte line cap); it is not in the diff and no ceiling moved. `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates` and `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests` are green on the head. No line on `main` outside the three files quotes any removed or reworded line (searched each phrase tree-wide), so no pin breaks.
- The four paid lines — right, no rule lost that anything on `main` relies on:
  - runbook old line 3 (file intro, "see SKILL.md, this file holds only detail") and the blank after it: dropped. It carried no seat rule; readers still arrive from SKILL.md lines 69, 246 and 326.
  - runbook old line 9 (a hand-hung `pm:blocking` is treated as a mislabel and the sweep corrects it against the index): dropped here, the rule survives at SKILL.md:120 (derived cache, never hung by hand), `triage-duties.md`:39–40 (the daily reconcile adds and removes it off `check-half-states` H14) and in H14's own finding text. Nothing in `scripts/pm` read the runbook line.
  - coordinator old line 3 (who reads the file; project seat see `seat-lifecycle.md`): dropped. The reader is named at SKILL.md:64 and in every section heading of the file; the project-seat pointer is at SKILL.md:78.
  - area-lease old line 3 (who reads the file; write only what is special to this mode, name the rest, never copy): the reader half survives at SKILL.md:97. The authoring half (never copy) has no other home in the skill; it bound authors of the file, no seat and no script, and the ratchet at headroom 0 still prices a copied rule. Accepted as dropped.
- Rule A, the seat may now narrow a card to the measured surface as a clear change method (runbook:150) — right, ordered by the card (item 1: the seat posts a `Premise corrected` comment that narrows the card). See ④ for the reading against runbook:152.
- Rule A, areas measure before the claim and areas and card threads re-check before code, stop and report to the seat (runbook:146, 147, 149) — right against the card and against SKILL.md:326 (the claim's `Premise:` line needs the reading before the claim is written).
- Rule B, the candidate line changes from "any time, card, priority, full order, suggested effort" to a batched message of one line per thread with seven fields, the coordinator opens the batch and answers every id at once (coordinator:24–26) — right against the card; priority, effort and the no-waiting-for-own-slot rule are all kept. One clause is wrong: S1.
- Rule B adds a prohibition the card's Change list does not spell out: areas and card threads never go to the coordinator directly (coordinator:25). Judged right: it is the direction area-lease:31 and runbook:141 already take (hand to the seat), and the PR body states it in the maintainer summary.
- Rule C, a card thread gains a write on its own PR body through the relay `issue_patch` (runbook:142) — wrong as landed: M1.

### ② Semver level

Nothing publishes: `.claude/**` only, no package, no changeset, label `skip-changeset`. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` stand on the PR body and match the claim; correct for a diff with no protocol surface. Check-runs: `Check Changeset` has two runs on this head, the first concluded failure (it ran before the label landed) and the later one concluded skipped, which is what `pr-automation.yml` does for a PR carrying `skip-changeset`. Every other run is success or skipped; none pending. Which of the two same-named runs the landing gate reads is the landing seat's reading, not a contract matter.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No dev report and no `open_questions`: the claim states the text was written in the area session itself, not by a dev subagent. That departs from area-lease:40 (writing goes through subagents) and is disclosed; it does not change what the text says. Left to the L1 read.
- Branch `claude/project-thread-2jkmek` instead of the issue-named form: the measured platform exception at runbook:139, stated in the claim.
- Tier: the claim routes the at-tier review of the governed text to the review seat; this record is that review.
- Rules and process text is on the human floor (`triage-duties.md`:92–93). The card quotes the maintainer's order for these three rules; the path is governed and lands by human approval either way.
- The claim's `Premise: holds` line says no line names who edits a card thread's PR body. That reading is false on `main`: its search covered `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch` only and missed `.claude/agents/os-dev.md`:66. Escalated as M1.
- The area's question (does narrowing at runbook:150 collide with the human floor at runbook:152): answered in ④, no collision, one nit.
- SQL push-down: not applicable, no code in the diff.

### ④ Design judgment

M1 (must-fix) — Rule C contradicts the text its own reader is bound to. runbook:142 tells the card thread to edit its own PR body through `issue_patch` and forbids asking the seat or the area. On `main`, `.claude/agents/os-dev.md`:66 says the dev writes the PR body only at `pr_create`, never by PATCH, names the change in its report, and the seat writes it through `seat-post-protocol.md`; os-dev.md:63 fixes the dev's write budget at three writes, and a body patch is a fourth. The card thread is the dev (runbook:131), it is required to read `os-dev.md` and forbidden to read SKILL.md, with references read only on demand (runbook:140). So the thread's mandatory text forbids exactly what the new line orders, and the new line forbids exactly what the mandatory text orders: a thread that follows `os-dev.md` reports and waits, a seat that follows the runbook does not write, and the body stays stale. `os-dev.md` already carries a card-thread exception where one is meant (line 32, the empty-branch probe); it carries none here. The card asked for this rule, so the rule stands; what fails is that it has two homes that disagree, against the card's own "one home, pointers where needed". Fix in this PR: give os-dev.md:66 (and the three-write budget at :63) the card-thread exception pointing at runbook:142, paid inside `os-dev.md` (405 of 405, line 66 already at 120 bytes). The header comment of `scripts/pm/fleet-write/dispatch.mjs` (the section on a PR body rewritten after round 1) states the same old rule; it enforces nothing about who sends, so it is a stale comment for a follow-up, not part of this finding.

S1 (should-fix) — coordinator:25 lets the dispatch order travel as "its full text or its file". runbook:136, untouched in this PR, says the order is written by the coordinator into the thread's opening message and is never landed in a shared directory, with a pointer left on the card. The old coordinator line said full text only. A seat reading both cannot tell whether an order file in the project files is allowed, and the plain reading of the new clause is that it is, which is the thing runbook:136 forbids. Either drop "or its file" (the "files to read" field at coordinator:24 already covers reference files), or change runbook:136 in the same PR with the ruling that allows it.

The collision question, runbook:150 against runbook:152 — no collision. Line 150 defines the clear change method as: target unchanged, and only a change of landing point or fix, or a narrowing to the measured surface. Line 152 then gives every other scope cut, downgrade and close to the human floor. The structure is an enumerated exception followed by "the rest", the same shape line 151 already had for ruling conflicts on `main`, and the exception is the one the card orders. The plain reading a seat takes: line 147 obliges it to measure each premise line including where the premise applies, so the measured surface is the part of the card the reading confirms, and narrowing drops only what the reading refuted; line 150 requires the comment to record the original premise, the reading and the change, so a dropped part is traceable and the L1 re-read at runbook:193 can check it. A part that reproduces, or that nobody measured, is not narrowed away under line 150; cutting it is line 152's and stays with the human (`triage-duties.md`:92, cutting a card in half). This matches what `os-dev.md`:385 already allowed a dev (a PR that covers only the surviving part).

Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract):
- N1: "measured surface" at runbook:150 can be misread as "whatever was measured" by a seat that skipped part of line 147. "The surface the reading confirms" would close that reading. The interpretation above is the one this record holds the line to.
- N2: runbook:149 ends in "the seat posts `Premise corrected`" with no condition. Read with lines 148 and 150–152 the seat still has three exits (correct the card, decision inbox, human floor); the line reads as if a correction always follows.
- N3: runbook:146 has the area measure before the claim; the area-lease:39 pointer says before code and sits after the claim lines (37–38). The home is the runbook and the pointer leads there, so the timing is recoverable, but an area reading only area-lease would measure after claiming.
- N4: coordinator:24 says batch and coordinator:25 says never wait for your own slot; no line says a single p1 candidate is a batch of one and is not held for company. coordinator:26 says the batch is opened whole and all ids answered at once, and in the same line that a full cap queues; the reply for queued rows is left unstated.
- N5: "areas and card threads never go to the coordinator directly" (coordinator:25) is unscoped; inside section three it reads as about thread requests, while the section five heading still says the coordinator receives a card thread's `needs_decision`. The seat route in `lanes/director.md`:23 already agrees with the new line.
- N6: runbook:142 names the op but not the body's signed last line (`seat-post-protocol.md`:30), and "only when the thread is closed" can be read to bar the seat's own body edits on an open thread (SKILL.md:323, `platform-readings.md`:289–290). Both writers send the whole body, so each must re-read before it writes. The relay's refusal names the trailer shape, so the first gap corrects itself.
- N7: when M1 is fixed, `os-dev.md`:385 (a falsified premise may end in a PR that covers only the surviving part) is worth one look beside runbook:149 (stop and report first).

Judged here: the change between `b898a12d` and this head (one commit, four files, +6/−6), the net diff against merge base 97defd6067 (four files, +12/−12), the four files whole at this head, card #34625 with its claim 6937847756 and the amendment 6938383525, the PR body, the final-head comment 6938556347, and the 47 check-runs on this head. ### ① Derived judgments

- os-dev.md:63 and :66 against runbook:142, both readers — right. A dev subagent reads :63 (three writes: push, `pr_create`, report) and :66 (writes the PR body only at `pr_create`, never patches, the seat writes it); runbook:142 speaks only of the thread, so nothing there reaches the subagent. A card thread reads :63 (it additionally edits the body) and :66 (it edits its own under `dispatch-runbook.md`), follows the pointer under the on-demand rule of runbook:140, and finds at runbook:142 the op (relay `issue_patch`), the duty to report the key points, and the bar on asking the seat or the area. The mandatory text and the home now say the same thing, with the rule in one home and a pointer from the file the thread is bound to, the shape the card asked for. os-dev.md:67 (every write over budget is listed in `api_writes`) and execution-duties.md:140 (body writes go through the relay write tools) agree with it.
